newsitem.title: UK: UK Readicut optimistic despite strong pound.
newsitem.headline: UK Readicut optimistic despite strong pound.

text.p: Readicut International, the British specialist textiles manufacturer, said on Tuesday it remained cautiously optimistic it could strengthen its performance despite damage to its overseas competitiveness from a strong pound.
"The strength of sterling is threatening to suppress a recovery in manufacturing just as it was gaining momentum," chairman Charles Godwin said in a statement.
"We are feeling the effects in our export business and our competitive position in Continental Europe is being weakened."

The group earlier reported a small increase to first half pre-tax profits, which rose to 3.3 million pounds after 2.8 million pounds in same period last year, when the group took an exceptional charge of 1.24 million pounds.
But the company could afford to be cautiously bullish in its outlook with "good order books" in most of its businesses.

"We are determined to ensure that our investment in management, reorganisation and plant will before too long deliver the hoped for results and put Readicut in a position to move forward strongly," Godwin said.
Heavy investment costs and the acquisition of the Alan Farrow Group in the first six months led to higher interest rate charges and increased gearing, the company reported.

In addition, Readicut said start-up and restructuring costs suffered by three loss-making businesses dragged down first-half profits, but "a speedy resolution to their problems will have a very positive impact on our future results".
